threads.1883: Keynes is born the year Krakatoa erupts. Bolton will not be born for another 67 years, Smith for another 70.
threads.1886: Gold is found on the Witwatersrand. Fifty years later, mining shares make up about two-thirds of Keynes's King's fund.
threads.1914: The Stock Exchange shuts for five months. Keynes, 31, writes up the City's crisis and joins the Treasury a few months later.
threads.1925: Britain goes back on gold at the pre-war rate; Keynes attacks the decision in print the same year.
threads.1931: Britain leaves gold. Around the same time, Keynes stops trying to time the market and starts picking shares.
threads.1936: The General Theory comes out in February, the Arts Theatre opens the same month, and Keynes's own wealth reaches its peak.
threads.1946: Keynes dies in April. Bolton is born four years later; their lives never overlap.
threads.1974: UK shares lose half their value. Bolton is three years into his City career; Smith, 21, graduates from Cardiff.
threads.1975: The year after the worst fall, UK shares more than double: +152%.
threads.1979: Exchange controls are abolished in October; in December Bolton launches Special Situations.
threads.1992: Smith is sacked for exposing accounting tricks the year the Cadbury Report sets new rules on how companies are run.
threads.2007: Bolton hands over his fund at the end of the year Northern Rock's run starts the financial crisis.
threads.2010: Two launches in one year: Bolton's China trust in April, Smith's Fundsmith Equity in November.
threads.2014: Bolton retires in April; in September Smith leaves Tullett Prebon to focus on Fundsmith.
threads.2026: The FTSE 100 closes above 10,000 for the first time, on 5 January.

crossings.d: Stepping back from his fund, Bolton sets out his lessons in The Spectator under a headline invoking the wisdom of Keynes and Mark Twain.
Bolton launches Fidelity China Special Situations in April; Smith launches Fundsmith Equity on 1 November.
Bolton retires from running money in April; Smith leaves Tullett Prebon in September to focus on Fundsmith.

storms.name: The exchange shuts
storms.what: As war approaches, the London Stock Exchange closes on 31 July 1914 and stays shut for five months.
storms.M: Aged 31, a Cambridge economist. He writes an account of the City's crisis and joins the Treasury in January 1915.
storms.B: Not yet born.
storms.L: Not yet born.

storms.name: The post-war slump
storms.what: The post-war boom collapses. UK shares lose 9.3% in 1920 and unemployment soars.
storms.M: Speculating in currencies with borrowed money, he is wiped out by May 1920. By the end of 1922 he has cleared his debts.
storms.B: Not yet born.
storms.L: Not yet born.

storms.name: The Great Crash
storms.what: The Hatry fraud shakes London in September 1929, Wall Street crashes in October and the slump spreads. UK shares fall three years running; Britain leaves the gold standard in 1931.
storms.M: Commodity losses cut his own net worth to under £8,000. His King's fund falls 14.2% and 11.5% in the years to August 1930 and 1931, less than the market.
storms.B: Not yet born.
storms.L: Not yet born.

storms.name: The 1937-38 fall
storms.what: Recession, rearmament and the road to war. UK shares lose 15.7% in 1937 and 9.2% in 1938.
storms.M: His fortune falls from over £500,000 to under £200,000 and his King's fund loses 22.6% in the year to August 1938. He stays invested and explains why in his May 1938 memo.
storms.B: Not yet born.
storms.L: Not yet born.

storms.name: Britain alone
storms.what: War, Dunkirk and the Battle of Britain. UK shares lose 6.8% in 1940.
storms.M: Joins the Treasury as an adviser in August 1940. His King's fund loses 5.9% in the year to August 1940, while the index loses 18.8%.
storms.B: Not yet born.
storms.L: Not yet born.

storms.name: The 1973-74 crash
storms.what: An oil shock, a secondary banking crisis, the three-day week and soaring inflation. UK shares lose 28.7% in 1973 and 51.8% in 1974, then gain 152.1% in 1975.
storms.M: Died in 1946.
storms.B: In his early twenties at the merchant bank Keyser Ullman, learning the trade in the worst market since at least 1900.
storms.L: Graduates from Cardiff with a First in 1974 and starts his career at Barclays.

storms.name: Black Monday
storms.what: Days after the Great Storm hits southern England, markets crash around the world. The FTSE 100 falls more than a fifth in two days, yet UK shares still end the year up 8.4%.
storms.M: Died in 1946.
storms.B: Eight years into running Special Situations.
storms.L: Rated the top banking analyst in London.

storms.name: The dot-com bust
storms.what: The internet bubble bursts. The FTSE 100 halves from its peak at the end of 1999 to March 2003.
storms.M: Died in 1946.
storms.B: Had refused internet shares and lagged the market by almost 20% in the boom. The bust proves him right.
storms.L: Floats Collins Stewart on the stock market in 2000, as chief executive.

storms.name: The financial crisis
storms.what: Northern Rock suffers the first run on a British bank in over a century. In 2008 Lehman Brothers fails and the government rescues the big banks.
storms.M: Died in 1946.
storms.B: Hands over his fund at the end of 2007 and moves to mentoring.
storms.L: Chief executive of Tullett Prebon, a broker between banks.

storms.name: The COVID crash
storms.what: Lockdown. UK shares fall 36% in 46 trading days and end the year down 9.8%.
storms.M: Died in 1946.
storms.B: Retired from fund management since 2014.
storms.L: Fundsmith Equity gains 18.3% in the year, against 12.3% for world shares.

storms.name: The gilt crisis
storms.what: Inflation tops 10%, and September's mini-budget sends gilt yields soaring until the Bank of England steps in. UK shares end the year up 0.3%.
storms.M: Died in 1946.
storms.B: Retired.
storms.L: Fundsmith Equity loses 13.8%, against a 7.8% fall for world shares.

about: A year-by-year record of three British investors' lives, from Keynes's birth in 1883 to today, set against what was happening in Britain and the world.
Their lives never overlap: Keynes died in 1946 and Bolton was born in 1950. Seeing them on one line shows how the same storms, and the same lessons, come round again.
Each year shows how old each man was, where he was in life, what he did, and the big events around him: prime ministers, wars, crashes and inventions.
Only the three of them. Nothing here is about the person who built the library.
method: Keynes: the Oxford Dictionary of National Biography, King's College, his own memo and letters, and Chambers and Dimson's research on the King's College archive.

Bolton and Smith: their own books and articles, Fidelity and Fundsmith documents, and the trade press, cross-checked with Wikipedia. Where sources disagree on a year (for example when Smith started at Barclays), we give the range or leave the exact year out.

Market numbers: UK shares from Cambridge Associates' long-run series (1900-2017) and published FTSE All-Share total returns since; Keynes's fund from Chambers and Dimson's yearly table (years ending in August); Fundsmith from its own factsheets. Year-by-year figures for Bolton's fund are not published in a source we could check, so they are not shown.
World events are summarised from the standard historical record. Ages are the age each man reaches in that year.
All summaries are in our own words. Exact quotes are short, in quotation marks, and come from the named source.
